thesis: India's lead-acid leader (Amaron) at a price the engine's own ladder calls investable: Rs 734 sits 30% below the Rs 1,044 INV trigger and 51% below the Rs 1,512 DCF fair value, with every gate green — zero pledge, Z'' 6.98 safe, E1-E6 clean, no event vetoes. The market is pricing the margin trough (OPM 11% vs 14% two years ago), two straight years of PAT decline, and a Rs 1,500 cr+/yr lithium-capex program that bleeds cash while the new-energy segment still loses money. The quality flags are real but visible: FY26 PAT is flattered by ~Rs 300 cr of exceptional gains, and the DCF's 0%-payout assumption overstates sustainable growth. Even after haircutting for both, the valuation cushion is large — the question is whether lead-acid margins stabilize and the gigafactory executes, not whether the business is distressed.
